<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Establish a useful, embeddable Rust SDK and a thin standalone CLI for Unisphere before native telemetry normalization is shipped. The first shared operation resolves and validates explicitly supplied source-root configuration and returns structured diagnostics, so this delivery proves real SDK/CLI behavior rather than only compiling empty crates. Components must be independently executable against injected contracts and later composed; services do not wait for a finished CLI. Flowspace3 is the first intended consumer, not the owner of the public model. This product plan is prime-authored; a subsequently assigned PM owns implementation orchestration and peer composition through the reviewed guide.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- A Rust application can consume Unisphere as an ordinary in-process dependency and invoke real foundation behavior without a CLI subprocess, daemon, database or ML service.
- Humans and automation can install/run a thin CLI that exposes the same successful and failing foundation operations as the SDK with predictable output and exit behavior.
- Provide explicit configuration resolution/validation and actionable typed diagnostics as the first useful shared vertical slice, without prematurely selecting a native-session or telemetry persistence schema.
- Make independently testable services and adapters possible from agreed contracts, allowing PM-led parallel construction and later composition without an artificial finished-CLI prerequisite.
- Establish reproducible local build, test, architecture and smoke evidence plus developer-facing SDK/CLI documentation; adapt useful Flowspace3 code with preserved provenance rather than copy its server architecture.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Shipping a native session reader, harness discovery sweep, normalization pipeline, historical ingestion or Flowspace3 integration in Plan001; those need separate accepted scope.
- Choosing or implementing the final telemetry/session record format, OTLP exporter, archive format, update/rewind semantics, content/counts privacy profiles or durable cursor store in this foundation plan.
- A required daemon, HTTP/RPC service, Postgres/SQLite product store, job queue, watcher, model provider, embeddings, pricing engine or git attribution integration.
- Registry publication, release automation beyond applicable local/CI proof, cloud deployment, machine-global installs/config changes, hook installation or real private transcript access.
- Promoting gitignored scratch reader experiments into shipping code or treating their provisional native-observation contract as the public SDK model; experimentation may proceed independently under the separately authorized scratch scope.
- Using Flowspace-specific error codes, configuration fields, truncation policies, PostgreSQL turn schema or summarization scheduling as Unisphere requirements.

<a id="research-context"></a>

## Research Context

Inputs: requirements-spine.md (RQ-001–017); original-ask.md; assets/research/otel-common-format.md; pending first-consumer interview assets/requirements/flowspace3-interview.md. Flowspace3 source was reviewed for pure configuration resolution, structured error/envelope behavior, audience-aware output and kind-aware architecture checks. Reuse candidates: crates/core/src/config.rs, catalog.rs, envelope.rs and output.rs; crates/cli/src/render; crates/testkit/src/arch.rs and spawn.rs. Adapt only the parts needed for this product: its daemon/store/ML stack is outside scope. MIT licence in Flowspace3 LICENSE requires retaining notices for substantial copies. OTLP JSONL is a Development-stage official telemetry file scheme, but choosing the eventual telemetry output is a separate workshop, not a dependency for foundation diagnostics.

<a id="testing-strategy"></a>

## Testing Strategy

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| approach | Build behavioral unit/contract tests for configuration resolution and diagnostics, an external-consumer SDK integration check, a real subprocess CLI smoke for success and failure, and a negative dependency-boundary check. Run them through the repository engineering harness once implementation supplies the canonical Rust lane. |
| rationale | The project currently has no product source or runnable product proof. Harness onboarding tests are not SDK proof. Pure tests alone cannot establish CLI/library parity, and an architecture diagram cannot catch a reverse dependency. |
| focus_areas | Explicit configuration precedence; empty/invalid configuration; deterministic diagnostics; SDK/CLI semantic parity; machine/human rendering; caller-controlled side effects; injected service independence; clean checkout consumption; negative dependency drift; sealed temporary HOME/config/fixtures. |
| excluded | Native reader correctness, telemetry schema compatibility, collector round trips, real vendor stores and pricing are not Plan001 acceptance. Scratch experiment tests remain separate and cannot make foundation ACs pass. |
| mock_usage | Prefer injected deterministic fakes and temporary filesystem fixtures at real variation boundaries; use real Rust caller/CLI composition for integration. Do not introduce a trait or mocking framework solely to satisfy a plumbing assertion. |

<a id="risks-assumptions"></a>

## Risks & Assumptions

Foundation-only scope was explicitly selected by Jordan. The first real operation is configuration inspection/validation, not a fake reader or a claim that telemetry collection works. Assume an explicitly supplied configuration document and caller overrides are sufficient initially; do not silently import ambient user configuration. The exact configuration shape, SDK/CLI signatures, crate topology, worker units/waves and code-level checks belong to the reviewed implementation guide. The outstanding Flowspace3 interview can refine later reader integration but does not block an independent library/configuration foundation. Product intent ready does not imply guide approval, baseline sealing, dispatched peers or any completed AC.

<a id="risks"></a>

## Risks

| risk | likelihood | impact | mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| An SDK-shaped crate merely forwards to the CLI/server, making embedded use and independent development impossible. | Medium | High | External Rust caller proof and service-only tests must succeed without a CLI subprocess/server; forbid reverse dependency edges. |
| Copying Flowspace3 imports its database/ML dependencies, global configuration assumptions or product-specific policies. | High | High | Adapt a documented minimal reuse set, retain licences, review dependency boundaries and exclude server/indexing policies. |
| A foundation implementation becomes only empty crates and help/version output. | Medium | High | Require the same real configuration-resolution/diagnostic operation through external SDK invocation and installed CLI success/error smoke. |
| Undecided telemetry format or pending consumer preferences stall all component development. | Medium | Medium | Keep telemetry readers/format selection out of Plan001; specify foundation interfaces in the guide so independent services/CLI/tests can proceed and compose later. |
| Tests or diagnostics read actual HOME, credentials or native sessions and pass only on one developer machine. | Medium | High | Explicit injected settings, sealed subprocess environments and temporary fixtures; verify the foundation leaves external state untouched. |
| Builder-generated converter guide is mistaken for Unisphere architecture. | High | High | Known harness defect row 37: the populated teaching guide remains unapproved and must be replaced during the real guide stage, never used for dispatch. |

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Prime owns initial product intent; PM owns later implementation orchestration, peer packets and assembled delivery. Planning does not appoint a runtime prime or release implementation.
- Use the reviewed guide to define contracts before fan-out; release independent components together where their true dependencies allow it. Services must not depend on a completed CLI or same-wave sibling implementation.
- Use first-class harness Builder allocation/readiness/dispatch/composition operations and report dogfood problems to pij-varied-alpaca; never replace failed gates with assumptions or bypasses.
- The permanent orphan governance branch remains separate; canonical product plan/guide/code/evidence stay on the product plan branch. Direct plan authoring does not mutate canonical flow state.
- No generated task, plan AC, contract baseline, review or proof receipt is marked complete before actual applicable evidence exists.
- Scratch native readers are separately authorized experiments, gitignored and not imported by shipping crates; promotion requires later accepted product scope and review.
